Treatment summary
The patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with
complaints of neck and low back pain. The mechanism of injury is consistent with the
reported symptoms, and the force involved is in keeping with a cervical and lumbar
strain. Over the course of care the patient attended 33 visits, with near-daily
attendance for much of that period. Several additional body regions were added to the
treatment plan a number of weeks after the collision. Cervical and lumbar imaging was
unremarkable, and orthopeidc and neurological examinations were within normal limits.
Nearly all of the reported findings rest on the patient's own description of pain and
function. No prior injury to the cervical or lumbar spine is documented in available
records. Billing reviewed for this episode shows no duplicate or repeated charges for
the same services. Recommendations include a graduated return to usual activities, a
home exercise program, and reassessment of the treatment frequency at the next
scheduled review.
